s: The family tree of Jesus from Abraham through David. Joseph learns in a dream that Mary's child is from the Holy Spirit, and Jesus is born.
Wise men from the east follow a star to worship the child. Joseph takes the family to Egypt to escape Herod, then settles in Nazareth.
John the Baptist preaches repentance. Jesus is baptized, and the Father's voice says: This is my beloved Son.
Jesus is tempted in the desert for forty days. He begins to preach and calls his first disciples, fishermen by the sea of Galilee.
The Sermon on the Mount begins: the Beatitudes. You are the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Love your enemies.
Give alms, pray and fast in secret. Jesus teaches the Our Father. Do not worry about tomorrow; seek first the kingdom of God.
Do not judge. Ask and it will be given you. Build your house on rock by doing what Jesus says.
Jesus heals a leper, a centurion's servant and Peter's mother-in-law, and calms a storm.
Jesus forgives and heals a paralysed man and calls Matthew the tax collector. He raises a girl and heals the sick.
Jesus sends out the twelve apostles to preach and warns them of persecution.
Jesus praises John the Baptist. Come to me, all you who labour, and I will give you rest.
Jesus is Lord of the sabbath. The Pharisees accuse him of working with Satan's power.
Parables of the kingdom: the sower, the weeds, the mustard seed, the hidden treasure and the pearl.
John the Baptist is beheaded. Jesus feeds five thousand and walks on the water.
Jesus teaches what truly defiles a person. He heals a Canaanite woman's daughter and feeds four thousand.
Peter confesses that Jesus is the Christ, and Jesus gives him the keys of the kingdom. Jesus foretells his death.
Jesus is transfigured on the mountain before Peter, James and John. He heals a boy and pays the temple tax.
Who is the greatest in the kingdom? Become like little children. Forgive seventy times seven.
Jesus teaches on marriage and blesses children. The rich young man goes away sad.
The parable of the workers in the vineyard. Jesus came not to be served but to serve. Two blind men are healed.
Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey and drives the sellers out of the temple. Parables of two sons and the wicked tenants.
The parable of the wedding feast. Render to Caesar. The greatest commandment is to love God and neighbour.
Jesus denounces the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees and weeps over Jerusalem.
Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple and his coming at the end of the age.
Parables of the ten virgins and the talents. At the last judgment: whatever you did to the least of these, you did to me.
Jesus is anointed at Bethany. At the Last Supper he gives his body and blood. He prays in Gethsemane, is arrested, and Peter denies him.
Judas despairs. Jesus is tried before Pilate, mocked, crucified and buried.
Jesus rises from the dead and sends the apostles to make disciples of all nations: I am with you always.

1: An angel tells Joseph that Mary's child is from the Holy Spirit and is to be named Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.
2: Gentiles from the east come to worship the newborn king. From the start, Jesus comes for all nations.
3: At Jesus' baptism the Spirit descends and the Father speaks. Father, Son and Holy Spirit are revealed together.
4: For forty days Jesus faces the devil's temptations and overcomes them with the word of God, where Israel once failed in the desert.
5: Jesus begins the Sermon on the Mount with the Beatitudes, his portrait of true happiness in God's kingdom.
6: Jesus teaches his disciples the Lord's Prayer, the prayer of all Christians.
16: Jesus makes Simon the rock on which he will build his Church and gives him the keys of the kingdom. The Church sees here the role of Peter and his successors, the popes.
17: Jesus' glory shines out on the mountain with Moses and Elijah, strengthening the apostles before his passion.
26: Jesus gives his body and blood under the signs of bread and wine. This is the institution of the Eucharist, celebrated at every Mass.
27: Jesus dies on the cross for the sins of the world. The veil of the temple tears in two: the way to God is open.
28: Jesus rises from the dead on the third day, as he said. Everything in the Christian faith rests on this event.
The risen Jesus sends his apostles to make disciples of all nations and baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

27: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

Jesus is not saying that God has abandoned him. These are the opening words of [[Psalm 22|psalms/22/2]]. In ancient Jewish teaching and oral tradition, standard practice called for referencing an entire Psalm by invoking its first line. Reciting the opening line was intended to direct listeners to the full text and context of the passage. In that Psalm, there’s a mocking crowd, the pierced hands and feet, the soldiers casting lots for his garments. Jesus is showing that the Scripture is being fulfilled in him. Psalm 22 does not end in despair. It transitions from anguish to praise, ending with God delivering the sufferer and establishing his kingdom across all nations.
